newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ARRIETA SAYS OPEC SHOULD MAKE REVENUE TOP PRIORITY.
newsitem.headline: ARRIETA SAYS OPEC SHOULD MAKE REVENUE TOP PRIORITY.

text.p: Venezuelan Oil Minister Erwin Arrieta on Tuesday said that key to OPEC's future was how to maximise revenues rather than a simple focus on output quotas.
"Revenue is the key," Arrieta told Reuters in the lobby of his hotel ahead of Wednesday's OPEC meeting.
"(Output quotas) are not the only point. If our strategy is to establish a ceiling it should be considered together with a number of other factors that we have been ignoring for years."

Venezuela already appears to be following a strategy to maximise export revenues regardless of the impact on oil prices. It is OPEC's largest quota violator, recently pumping as much as 800,000 barrels per day (bpd) in excess of its 2.359 million allocation.
Actual OPEC output is running some two million bpd in excess of the official 25.03 million ceiling.

Arrieta said he expected OPEC on Wednesday would discuss a plan he presented a year ago to the producer group suggesting a change in the group's strategy toward oil markets. The minister wants a regional approach and has said OPEC should exclude domestic consumption from quota measurement.
"The market is out of control. Let's get the market back to the real actors -- the producers and consumers," he said.
State Venezuelan oil company Petroleos de Venezuela has called on OPEC to abandon quotas in favour of boosting revenues by maximising market share.
But Arrieta, arriving in Vienna on Monday, said it was not his country's aim to push for an end to OPEC's quota system.
